settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: digester.setValidating(false) is set (CcmParser.java:88), which disables DTD validation but does not by itself disable external entity resolution.
Newer Commons Digester releases historically enabled some secure-processing defaults; the effective behavior depends on the resolved transitive version, which is not shown in the read pom.xml lines.
No source line in the read spans explicitly enables entity resolution or shows attacker-controlled content being reflected, so exploitation is not demonstrated from source alone.
candidates.description: CcmParser.parseCCMXmlFile(InputStream) creates a new org.apache.commons.digester.Digester, sets setValidating(false) and a ClassLoader, registers bean-property setters, and then calls digester.parse(ccmXmlFile). No XXE-relevant hardening is applied: there is no digester.setFeature("http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl", true), no disabling of http://xml.org/sax/features/external-general-entities / external-parameter-entities / load-external-dtd, and no EntityResolver. Commons Digester delegates to the underlying SAX parser; a report file containing a DOCTYPE with external entity declarations would therefore be parsed with the parser's default entity behavior. The untrusted input is the CCM report file discovered and read by the build: CcmPublisher passes the configured pattern to FilesParser with a CcmParser instance (CcmPublisher.java:96-97), and CcmReporter likewise parses 'ccm.xml' via CcmParser (CcmReporter.java:132-133); the parser wiring calls digester.parse at CcmParser.java:106. Impact, if entities are resolved, is XML External Entity (file disclosure / SSRF) on the Jenkins controller or agent. This is reported as a candidate: the actual effective entity behavior depends on the Digester/SAX/JDK version resolved transitively (pom.xml only declares analysis-core 1.94 and inherits an analysis-pom 1.63 parent; the digester version is not visible in the read lines), which I could not verify.
missing_evidence: The Commons Digester version actually resolved by the build (not present in the read pom.xml lines; only analysis-core 1.94 and analysis-pom 1.63 parent are visible).
Whether AbstractAnnotationParser (analysis-core) or the FilesParser path performs any additional XML hardening before delegating to CcmParser.parse.
Runtime configuration of the underlying SAX parser (secure processing default in the target JDK).
Any reference to the testXxe-*.xml fixtures in test code: search_text for 'testXxe' and 'xxe' returned no hits, and the read test files (CCMParserTest, DefaultHandlerTest) do not reference them.
preconditions: A build (or an attacker able to place a report file matching the configured Ant pattern, e.g. **/*.cs, in the workspace) supplies a CCM report XML that is fed to CcmParser.
Analysis is published via CcmPublisher.perform (FilesParser + CcmParser) or CcmReporter.perform.
The Commons Digester / SAX / JDK version in the dependency tree does not already disable external entities/DTD loading by default.
candidates.title: CcmParser parses build-supplied XML with Apache Commons Digester without disabling external entities (potential XXE)
